line: In politics. Mark Levine, who oversees New York City's pension funds, asked anthro-pic to delay its stock market debut and deal with A I safety first.
In finance. Insurance against tech firms failing to repay reached record prices, as fears grow over A I debt, with data centre firm CoreWeave hit hardest.
In infrastructure. Taiwan's chip giant T S M C says it is in talks to join Tesla boss Elon Musk's planned chip plant in Texas, but only if T S M C runs it.
In robotics. Swedish car maker Volvo plans to let its cars drive hands-free on local roads with N-vidia's A I, handling traffic lights and turns while the driver keeps watch.
In tech. Meta has released a very large open-weight A I model built to run on Apple's Mac computers, though it needs at least a terabyte of memory.
In the lab. Physicists from Harvard and Google DeepMind found that an OpenAI coding agent solved ninety eight percent of their new research problems with no human help.
In law. The U S consumer watchdog ordered OpenAI and anthro-pic to hand over records of A I safety incidents, as it investigates them.
And finally, for fun. M I T researchers gave A I agents lobster bodies on a virtual island, and they built temples and invented their own games.
Also in the full report. Cameroon bans young pupils from using A I chatbots. And outside safety testers get the same access to anthro-pic's models as its own staff.
And for the bigger picture: demand for A I is strong, but its borrowing is getting more expensive. Watch Meta's results on Wednesday to see if big A I spending holds. This is not financial advice.
